name: container_sync_tickcost_lowend
about: The weak-host tick cost of a consumer that refuses every record, old code against next code at the same time under the same load. Two weak consumer hosts, r1w-02 on tree old and r1w-03 on tree next, both limited to 0.35 CPU before their apps exist; each runs two consumer apps of set tc (key lnet-sync-tc), one without a secret and one with the secret of another set (s9), and each app gets 1,000 received-history entries. The provider on r1w-01 (next) publishes with the set's secret s1 every 90 s, so both hosts refuse every record (old: the format line for both apps; next: the format line for the app without a secret, the mac line for the other) and every 10 s tick of each app reads its whole history. Measured per host from its probe over the 1,200 s window 'refusing' (it starts 240 s after the provider's create, after the first refusal): the mean wall time of a process call of its two container app runner instances (the core's own process timer, pooled; each call runs the app's sync tick every 10 s), its main-loop rate and its node process CPU. Pass: on r1w-03 (next) the mean process time and the CPU at most 1.10 x r1w-02's (old), the main-loop rate at least 0.90 x. The same figures over the 600 s window 'idle' (apps seeded, no record yet) are recorded, to show any difference between the two hosts that exists without refusals. Init with --arm next --arm-of r1w-02=old --workers 3 --docker-nodes r1w-01,r1w-02,r1w-03; needs the image redis:7-alpine on this machine.

refusing.r1w-03: record mac does not match this node's sync secret
